01 / THE BASICS

Two ways to plug in.

The battery stores direct current (DC). With AC charging, the car’s onboard charger converts alternating current into DC. A DC fast charger does that conversion outside the car.

AC or DC? See the difference.

Alternating current. Electricity is converted into DC inside the car, then stored in the battery. Usually suited to longer stops, such as charging overnight.

Direct current. Electricity is converted inside the charging station and delivered to the battery as DC. Often faster, when your EV supports it.

HOME · AC

Charge while you park.

Usually the simplest routine: connect to an approved home charger overnight. Charging is limited by your electrical supply, charger and the car’s onboard AC rating.

PUBLIC · AC OR DC

Top up along the way.

Public AC suits longer stops. DC is useful on trips when your car supports it. A higher number on the charger does not mean your vehicle can accept that much power.

02 / SPEEDS & PLUGS

Match the plug to your EV.

Check the exact vehicle variant and charging manual. Connector compatibility and charging power are separate things.

Two-wheelers usually use much smaller batteries and manufacturer-approved chargers. Some support dedicated fast charging or removable batteries; many do not. Never assume a car charger or a generic adapter will work.

03 / AT HOME

Start with a safe installation.

Your parking space

Have an authorised installer check sanctioned load, cable length, earthing, weather protection and a dedicated circuit with the required electrical protection. A faster wallbox may need a load upgrade; higher AC powers can need three-phase supply.

Apartment living

Agree the parking location, cable route, metering and billing with your RWA or housing society. Ask the DISCOM about supply capacity or a separate connection. Shared chargers may need load management and an agreed usage policy.

What to budget

A charger and basic installation may be included with the vehicle. If not, an indicative planning allowance is ₹25,000–₹70,000 for a basic AC wallbox and straightforward installation. Long cable runs, civil work and supply upgrades can cost extra. Get an itemised site quote.

Everyday care

Use approved equipment; avoid extension boards and improvised adapters. Keep plugs and cables undamaged, follow weather ratings and never connect flooded or damaged equipment. If a connector gets unusually hot or smells burnt, stop charging safely and contact service.

Installation figures are budgeting examples, not a national tariff or a quoted offer. Your electrician and DISCOM must confirm suitability. For removable batteries, use the maker’s charger in a ventilated location away from exits and combustible materials.

Charging time

Plan how long to stay plugged in.

Use the lower of charger power and your vehicle’s accepted charging power. Assumes 90% power-to-stored-energy efficiency; does not model a charging curve.

Public operators may meter at the charger output rather than at the supply. Losses and billed units therefore differ; this calculator uses one transparent 90% assumption. Parking, idle, session fees and any taxes not included in your unit rate are extra. Real time depends on the vehicle, temperature, battery state, shared power and charging curve; especially above 80%, allow longer.

A practical comparison

A 40 kWh battery going from 20% to 80% stores 24 kWh. At 90% efficiency, that takes about 26.7 kWh from the supply: roughly ₹213 at ₹8/unit at home, or ₹533 at ₹20/unit publicly. These are example rates, not city-specific tariffs.

05 / ON THE HIGHWAY

A little planning. A smoother trip.

Build charging stops around your route and your real-world range, not just the advertised figure.

  1. Before you leave

    Check connector compatibility, access hours, operator payment options and recent status in the operator’s app. Identify a backup charger before you need it.

  2. Keep a buffer

    High speeds, hills, passengers, air-conditioning and weather change consumption. Aim to arrive with a comfortable reserve—often 15–20%, more on uncertain routes.

  3. Make the stop count

    Use the manufacturer’s battery preconditioning feature if available. A top-up to around 80% can be quicker than waiting for 100%; charge higher when the next leg needs it. Move the car when finished.

A FEW COMMON QUESTIONS

Good to know.

Can I use a normal household socket?

Only if the manufacturer permits it and an electrician confirms a dedicated, correctly rated, earthed outlet and protection. A socket that fits is not proof that the wiring is suitable for hours of continuous load.

Do I need to charge to 100% every day?

Follow your vehicle’s manual: battery chemistry and calibration requirements differ. Many vehicles allow a daily charge limit; some recommend periodic full charges. Avoid applying one rule to every EV.

Can I charge in the rain?

Approved outdoor equipment is designed for its stated weather rating. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions, keep connectors clear of standing water, and do not charge with damaged equipment or after flooding until inspected.

Will a 120 kW charger charge my car at 120 kW?

Only if the car can accept that power and conditions allow it. The battery-management system limits the rate, which often drops as the battery fills. Shared chargers can also split power between vehicles.

Why does charging slow down near full?

The battery-management system reduces current to protect cells and balance them. The last part of a charge can take disproportionately longer; a constant-power estimate cannot predict this accurately.

Can I own an EV without home charging?

It can work if reliable workplace or nearby public charging fits your routine. Before buying, check access, compatibility, typical waiting time and total cost. Try the routine rather than relying on a charger icon alone.

Can rooftop solar charge my EV?

Yes, through a properly installed electrical system and compatible charger. Direct solar use depends on daytime generation and when the EV is plugged in. An ordinary grid-connected solar system generally shuts down during an outage unless designed with backup.

Does fast charging damage the battery?

Vehicles manage charging to protect their batteries, but frequent high-power charging and heat can affect ageing. Follow your manufacturer’s charging guidance and warranty conditions; use slower charging when convenient.
